scope: Proposition 2.1 (A prime reservoir in a fixed progression) of the manuscript “Simultaneous primitive roots: a conditional lower bound for prime bases” (preprints/Simultaneous-primitive-roots-a-conditional-lower-bound-for-prime-bases-October-4-2026/simultaneous-primitive-roots-conditional-lower-bound-prime-bases.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 029 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0f36acf08bd34758), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume Inputs 4.1, 5.1, and 5.2. Let M ≥ 1 be odd and squarefree, and let a be a residue class modulo M with gcd(a(a − 1), M) = 1. There are constants cM,a > 0 and xM,a > 1 such that, for every real x ≥ xM,a, at least cM,ax/L2 primes p satisfy x < p < 2x, p ≡ a (mod M), p = 4rQ + 1, where r is a positive integer, Q > x0.9 is prime, and exp(L0.1 ) < ℓ < exp(L0.3 ) for every prime ℓ | r. The case M = 1 is included.
